title: Ivo and the Will
premise: Retired detective Emrys Yarrow, now keeping a failing bookshop afloat, is paid an absurd retainer by a nervous solicitor to prove that Aldous Vane, the town's beloved philanthropist, will not be murdered at his own anniversary dinner. The catch: the only evidence is a will, rewritten in secret, naming a beneficiary who has been dead for eleven years — the same year Emrys's late husband died in a fall everyone called an accident. As she digs, Emrys discovers her husband's death and Vane's fortune are braided together by a cover-up she once helped close. To stop a murder that hasn't happened yet, she must reopen the case that destroyed her career and decide whether justice belongs to the law or to the living.
about_author: X. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent fifteen years reading other people's last words before writing any of their own. They live above a bookshop they refuse to confirm is fictional.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Emrys Yarrow, dusting unsold stock in her failing bookshop, receives a visit from solicitor Halloran, who pays six months' fees upfront: prove that Aldous Vane will not be murdered at his anniversary dinner. No body, no threat, no evidence — just a rewritten will naming a dead woman. Emrys takes the money out of pride. POV: Emrys. Beat: wary curiosity masking old grief.

chapters.title: A Will Without a Grave
chapters.summary: In the archive room, Emrys studies the new will: the mysterious beneficiary is 'Mara Quill,' deceased eleven years — the same year her husband Daniel fell from the quarry ridge. Halloran claims he drew it up under instruction he cannot disclose. POV: Emrys. Beat: the first cold drop of recognition; this isn't a job, it's a door she sealed shut.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Emrys recalls the three 'accidents' she quietly solved after retirement, establishing her methods and reputation among those who know. Her old colleague DS Ferro warns her off anything touching the Quill file. POV: Emrys. Beat: competence and loneliness; we see why she can't walk away.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Emrys attends a charity preview of Vane's estate, cataloguing suspects: his brittle second wife Odile, resentful son Casper, devoted housekeeper Mrs. Ansel, and business partner Ruth Ibarra. Everyone performs happiness beautifully. POV: Emrys. Beat: social observation as detection; menace beneath civility.

chapters.title: What Mara Left Behind
chapters.summary: Emrys tracks down Mara Quill's surviving sister, Nell, who insists Mara never existed to the town — no records, no grave marker, just a rented room emptied overnight. Nell hands over a shoebox of letters signed only 'A.V.' POV: Emrys. Beat: tenderness and dread; the dead woman becomes a person.

chapters.title: The Quarry File
chapters.summary: Emrys pulls her copy of the closed file on Daniel's death and finds a page missing — the page bearing Mara Quill's name as a witness. She realizes she signed off on a report she no longer trusts. POV: Emrys. Beat: self-indictment; the detective discovers she may be part of the crime.

chapters.title: Casper's Debts
chapters.summary: Casper Vane, drunk and desperate, corners Emrys in her shop, certain someone is rewriting his inheritance and offering to sell information about his father's 'arrangements.' He mentions a name: Ferro. POV: Emrys. Beat: moral vertigo — the corruption reaches into the police.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Told partly through Mara's letters: she was Vane's accountant and discovered the philanthropy was laundering something uglier. She threatened to go public; then she vanished. POV: alternating Emrys and letter excerpts. Beat: rising horror; the past is more alive than the present.

chapters.title: Ferro's Warning
chapters.summary: DS Ferro comes to the bookshop after hours, not to threaten but to beg: reopening the Quill matter will destroy three families and Emrys herself. He reveals Daniel's death was investigated and buried from above. POV: Emrys. Beat: the law confesses its limits; loyalty curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Emrys engineers a meeting with Odile Vane, who is terrified of the anniversary dinner and nearly tells Emrys what she knows — until a phone call silences her mid-sentence. POV: Emrys. Beat: hope snatched away; the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Emrys reconstructs the missing file page from memory and a court transcription: Mara witnessed Daniel's fall — meaning Daniel knew what Mara knew. His death wasn't a fall; it was a message. POV: Emrys. Beat: devastation; grief reclassified as murder.

chapters.title: Mrs. Ansel's Silence
chapters.summary: The housekeeper, dying of illness and unafraid, tells Emrys that Mara didn't vanish — she was hidden, and someone in the house has been paying for her silence ever since. The will's beneficiary line is a promise being kept, or broken. POV: Emrys. Beat: reversal — the 'dead' beneficiary may be alive.

chapters.title: Halloran Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted, Halloran admits his client for the rewrite was Mara Quill herself, alive and hiding, preparing to claim her name and testimony at the anniversary dinner. Someone learned of the plan. The retainer was real: prevent the murder. POV: Emrys. Beat: the mystery pivots from whodunit to who-will.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Emrys races to find Mara before the dinner, following the letters' postmarks to a coastal cottage — arriving to find it searched and bloodless but recently lived-in. POV: Emrys. Beat: panic and resolve; the hunt compresses.

chapters.title: Ruth Ibarra's Ledger
chapters.summary: Business partner Ruth, believing Emrys is blackmailing Vane, shows her the true ledger: the philanthropy hid payments to keep witnesses quiet — including a standing payment to Ferro's old boss. Ruth wants Vane protected too, for her own reasons. POV: Emrys. Beat: every ally has an angle; power corrupts on all sides.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Emrys attends under a borrowed invitation. Toasts are raised; Odile's hand shakes; Casper drinks too much; a place card sits empty. Emrys reads the room like a crime scene waiting to happen. POV: Emrys. Beat: exquisite tension; the reader waits for the glass to fall.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara Quill walks into the dining room alive, and the dinner detonates. Vane stands, and for one moment looks less guilty than relieved — before the lights fail. When they return, Vane is dying on the floor and Mara is holding the knife she swears she never touched. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax begins; chaos and clarity colliding.

chapters.title: Who Swore It Closed
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Emrys works the locked room: the killer used the blackout and framed Mara. The evidence points to Ferro — until Emrys realizes the missing file page could only be taken by someone with access both then and now: Halloran, protecting the estate that funds his practice. POV: Emrys. Beat: the reveal; betrayal wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Confession at the Bookshop
chapters.summary: Emrys traps Halloran with the reconstructed page and Ruth's ledger, extracting his confession privately: he killed Daniel years ago on Vane's order and killed Vane now to bury both crimes. She records everything. POV: Emrys. Beat: cold triumph shadowed by cost; justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Price of Proof
chapters.summary: Ferro must choose: arrest Halloran on Emrys's illegally obtained evidence or let it go. He takes the confession and resigns rather than explain how he got it. Mara gives her testimony publicly; the estate unravels; Odile and Casper face ruin with strange relief. POV: Emrys. Beat: consequences distributed honestly; victory without vindication.

chapters.title: Daniel's Grave
chapters.summary: Emrys visits the quarry ridge and then the grave, finally able to say aloud what really happened. Mara joins her; two widows of the same crime. They agree the case is closed — truly this time. POV: Emrys. Beat: mourning completed; grief given its true shape.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the bookshop has customers again. A new client arrives with an impossible request, and Emrys — older, unburdened, still angry at the world — turns the sign to OPEN. POV: Emrys. Beat: quiet renewal; the detective chooses to keep choosing.
